text:
B: Hello. Martijn. Walthamstow.
A: Abena. Thornton Heath.
B: Did you do the puzzles at the start?
A: Yes. Some of them were badly made. The shapes.
B: The sequences too. One had two correct answers.
A: I didn't count. I just put something and moved on. You complained?
B: No. I'll put it in the survey.
A: Good. Somebody should tell them.
B: What do you do?
A: Senior care assistant. Residential home, older people, Norbury. Twelve-hour days.
B: How many a week?
A: Four, sometimes five. Depends on the rota. And the manager changes the rota whenever she likes, so you plan your week and then on Thursday it's different. That's what makes me tired. Not the work, the nonsense.
B: Yes. I'm a structural engineer. The work is fine. It's the meetings. People talking for an hour to avoid saying something won't work.
A: You tell them it won't work?
B: Yes. They don't like it.
A: [laughs] Same with me. A family asks how is mum, and the nurse says, oh, she's settling, she's doing lovely. She's not eating. So I tell them she's not eating. Then I'm the difficult one. You understand?
B: Yes. It's better they know.
A: Of course it's better. They are paying. They should know.
B: How many hours do you do in total?
A: About forty, forty-eight. You?
B: Fifty, fifty-five. Er, mostly my choice. I don't send drawings I'm not happy with.
A: Fifty-five and nobody makes you. That's your problem then.
B: [pause] Yes. My ex-wife said that.
A: Mm. Mine left for a woman from our church. So. Everybody has something.
B: Yes.
A: You have children?
B: A daughter, fourteen. Every other weekend and one night in the week.
A: My son is twenty-four, in Leicester. He calls on Sundays. When they are fourteen they don't talk to you. Then later they come back. Don't worry too much.
B: She's talking less, yes. Thank you.
A: Can I ask you something, since you do buildings?
B: Go on.
A: My landlord. I have a damp patch in the bathroom, on the ceiling near the corner, black, it comes back every time I clean it. He says it's my fault, I'm not opening the window. I open the window.
B: Is there an extractor fan?
A: There's one. It makes noise. I don't think it does anything.
B: Hold a sheet of toilet paper to it when it's on. If it doesn't pull the paper, it's not working. Also, is the patch on an outside wall, near the roof?
A: Yes. Top flat, it's the corner by the outside wall.
B: Then it could be cold bridging, or water getting in from the gutter or the roof. That's not condensation from your shower. Take photos with dates. Check after rain. If it's worse after rain, it's the building, and it's his job.
A: Hm. Toilet paper. I will do that tonight.
B: And write to him. Email, not phone.
A: I already write to him. He doesn't answer.
B: Then the council. Private sector housing team. They can inspect.
A: Okay. That's useful. Thank you. That's it.
